schema: Belavadös factions data with adventure hooks separated

provenance.policy: Faction data retained as Belavadös-native faction content; adventure hooks were separated into belavados_quest_hooks.json.

design_assumptions.mountain_underlayer_rule: All mountain settlements and mountain-dominant provinces include deep cavern settlement networks. Dwarves, tieflings, drow, shadow peoples, and related subterranean communities are present, especially in Drakmorren, Khorvaak, and Zharvokh.
design_assumptions.iazethas_rule: Iazethas is primarily dragon and dragonborn territory, with Valkhamesh influence and draconic law added to faction logic.
design_assumptions.thalryss_rule: Thalryss is a legal-crime pirate province. Its capital, Skulltide Expanse, is modeled as a floating ocean settlement made from retired pirate ships tied together with rope bridges and platforms.

lore_principles.campaign_tone: Dark steampunk fantasy/horror with rail, ferries, steamships, skyships, regulated portals, divine prisons, ichor economies, bureaucracy, and fragile peace.
lore_principles.faction_campaign_premise: Players begin at D&D 5e level 8 as competent peacekeepers or agents solving problems where trade, transit, divine prisons, cults, politics, and settlement rivalries overlap.
lore_principles.ledger_of_death: Nefarokir and the Ledger of Death make death records, inheritance, burial, identity, and stolen years central mission levers.
lore_principles.gods: The gods are imprisoned predators/creators whose ichor still sustains industries, cults, medicine, magic, and political power.
lore_principles.time_rule: Earth date/time is player-first; Belavadös civil date and sky-time are lore-second. Civil year is 11 months x 30 dates; astronomical year is 330.15 Belavadös solar days.
lore_principles.transport: Use trains, caravans, ferries, steamships, skyships, submarines for underwater settlements, and regulated portals instead of cars/planes.

time_conversion.core_rule: Earth dates/times first; Belavadös dates second for lore.

rivalries.public_reason: Licensing authorities and experimental academies disagree over risk tolerance.

rivalries.public_reason: Greenwatch blocks militarized infrastructure expansion through sacred sites.

rivalries.campaign_consequence: Choosing speed over protection can awaken encounters later.

rivalries.public_reason: Dragon legates want autonomy; Watchers monitor draconic treaty violations.

rivalries.public_reason: Peacekeepers suppress cult violence; cult cells frame suppression as proof civilization is a cage.

rivalries.campaign_consequence: Players can use cult intelligence without becoming useful to the cult.

rivalries.public_reason: Mire clans and root alliances disagree over who owns the memory of old battlefields.
rivalries.hidden_truth: Fungal witnesses and living roots remember different versions of the same divine imprisonment.
rivalries.campaign_consequence: Players may decide which memory becomes official history.
